record.original_question: In the appendix's adjacent-chain charge-density-wave model, what role does the multi-chain interaction and the added Peierls-gap term Δ′ play in forming a soliton-instanton configuration, and is that term necessary in order to obtain a sine-Gordon equation and therefore an instanton formulation?

evidence.quote:
What role does the multi chain argument play as far as formulation of the soliton – instanton ? Why
add in the Pierls gap term in the first place?

Punch line. Without the Pierls term added in, we do not get a Sine Gordon equation. No Instanton
formulation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a model of two adjacent one-dimensional charge-density-wave (CDW) chains coupled by an inter-chain interaction, with effective Lagrangian density containing: (i) the usual kinetic term for the CDW phase field φ(x,t) on each chain, (ii) an inter-chain coupling term that links the phase fields of the two chains, and (iii) an explicit Peierls-gap pinning term proportional to a parameter Δ′ that depends on cos φ (a Peierls/commensurability gap contribution). 

(a) Derive the Euler–Lagrange equation of motion for the relative phase field of the two coupled chains, retaining the Peierls-gap term Δ′. Show under what conditions this equation reduces to the sine-Gordon equation 
   ∂²φ/∂t² − c² ∂²φ/∂x² + (m²/β) sin(βφ) = 0, 
and identify the soliton (instanton) solution that interpolates between adjacent vacua of the cosine potential.

(b) Repeat the derivation with the Peierls-gap term Δ′ removed (Δ′ = 0). Determine whether the resulting equation of motion still admits a sine-Gordon form and, consequently, whether a soliton–instanton configuration of the same type can be constructed.

(c) Conclude precisely what role the multi-chain (inter-chain) interaction plays versus the role of the Peierls-gap term Δ′ in producing the sine-Gordon structure, and state whether inclusion of the Δ′ term is necessary to obtain an instanton formulation in this CDW setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved within the same source: without the Peierls (Δ′) gap term included in the Lagrangian, the equation of motion does not reduce to a sine-Gordon equation, so no instanton/soliton formulation of the standard sine-Gordon type is obtained. The multi-chain coupling alone is insufficient; the Peierls term provides the periodic cos-potential needed for sine-Gordon kink solitons. This is a standard result consistent with the Brazovskii–Kirova and Su–Schrieffer treatments of commensurate CDW solitons.

status_evidence.title: Solitons in conducting polymers / CDWs (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The sine-Gordon equation arises in models with a periodic cosine potential; without such a pinning potential the equation of motion is a free wave equation admitting no topological kink soliton.
status_evidence.claim: A periodic (Peierls-type) cosine potential term is required to obtain sine-Gordon kink/instanton solutions; pure linear inter-chain coupling without the cosine pinning term does not yield sine-Gordon.
